title: Zero-Downtime Database Secret Rotation with HashiCorp Vault
businessContext: SOC 2 compliance mandates that production PostgreSQL database passwords must rotate automatically every 30 days. Currently, when passwords are changed, all running application pods fail database health checks and crash, requiring a coordinated maintenance window.
problemStatement: Architect a zero-downtime database credential rotation pipeline using HashiCorp Vault Dynamic Database Secrets. Explain how Vault generates short-lived, unique user credentials per pod/service with dual-user rotation (User A and User B alternating), so that existing database connections remain active while new connections authenticate with rotated credentials.
constraints: Zero connection drops during credential rotation.
No hardcoded static database passwords in Kubernetes secrets or env vars.
Vault leases must automatically revoke credentials when TTL expires.
candidateTasks: Explain the dual-user rotation pattern: alternating active database roles without terminating in-flight queries.
Implement lease renewal ticker before TTL expires.
Gracefully drain and migrate connection pool when new credentials are issued.
hints: Vault creates unique dynamic database users: `v-token-app-172938...` with a configurable lease (e.g. 1 hour).
The application renews the lease periodically (`vault.renewLease()`). Before maximum TTL, it fetches new credentials and establishes a new pool, then drains the old pool.

testCases.name: Rotates credentials dynamically with zero connection drops

alternativeApproaches: AWS Secrets Manager automated rotation using Lambda and two-user rotation template (`user_master` alternates between `userA` and `userB`).
commonMistakes: Rotating the password immediately and dropping all active connections simultaneously.
Hardcoding a single database user across all microservices instead of role-based least privilege.
